themes.label: Critique of global stationarity in ARCH/regime-switching models
themes.need: A researcher questioning whether ARCH-type conditional-variance models truly capture volatility dynamics wants to know how unconditional-variance shifts can produce spurious ARCH effects and why Markov-switching-variance models still fail to relax global stationarity.

themes.label: Local-stationarity concept & homogeneity-interval procedure
themes.need: A researcher wants to understand what a homogeneity interval is (a period of locally constant statistical behavior) and the decision rule used to extend or terminate one when new observations arrive.
themes.distributed_justification: The introduction's homogeneity-interval concept (35-40) and its concrete Kolmogorov-Smirnov-functional decision procedure (83-84) serve one need; the intervening spectral-theory formalism (periodogram, Theorem 2.1) is assigned to its own theme.

themes.label: Spectral-domain goodness-of-fit theory: periodogram, Kiefer-Muller process, Theorem 2.1
themes.need: A researcher wants the spectral-domain theoretical machinery (periodogram, integrated periodogram, Kiefer-Muller process, Theorem 2.1) underlying a goodness-of-fit test for detecting changes in a time series' spectral distribution.
themes.distributed_justification: The homogeneity-interval decision procedure (own theme, 83-84) is interposed within the theoretical build-up; the surrounding periodogram-through-Theorem-2.1 narrative is one coherence unit resuming after it.

themes.label: Local ARMA(1,1) test on log-absolute returns: white-noise finding
themes.need: A researcher wants to know whether a locally-stationary ARMA(1,1) model fit to log-absolute S&P500 returns shows significant linear dependence within homogeneity intervals, or whether the data is white noise there.

themes.label: Piecewise-constant mean/variance model & volatility-regime findings
themes.need: A researcher wants the simplified piecewise-constant mean/variance model for log-absolute returns and the empirical volatility regimes (Depression era, oil crisis, recessions) it identifies over 1928-2000.

themes.label: Extending the method to absolute returns & post-1953 model
themes.need: A researcher wants to know how the homogeneity-interval method extends from log-absolute to absolute returns, and the simplified post-1953 constant-variance model that results.

themes.label: Robustness checks: constant-sigma, 1987 crash, t-statistic alternative
themes.need: A researcher wants robustness evidence for the constant-sigma assumption (including the October 1987 crash exception) and a comparison against a simpler t-statistic-based alternative test.

themes.label: Forecasting comparison: FARIMA long-memory vs shifts-in-mean model
themes.need: A researcher choosing between a stationary long-memory (FARIMA) model and the paper's non-stationary shifts-in-mean model wants to know which forecasts log-absolute S&P500 returns more accurately.
themes.distributed_justification: The introduction (41-44) poses the LM-vs-SM forecasting-comparison question that Section 4 (227-313) resolves in full; per the intro-poses/section-resolves pattern it joins that section's theme as a distributed span.
